title: 刚果医生夜班后承压：一晚就有患者死亡，为何国际援助仍未到位？
speaker: Declan Walsh

segments.en: Let me ask you lastly just about what you heard from that Congolese doctor with whom you spent the most time and I think in circumstances like this past outbreaks.
segments.zh: 最后，我想问你和那位刚果医生交流的情况。在过去的疫情中，医疗人员的沮丧和疲惫显而易见。

segments.en: The frustration and exhaustion are palpable among the medical staff who are in facilities like like this one.
segments.zh: 在这样设施中的医务人员，沮丧和疲惫是显而易见的。

segments.en: How would you assess his level of optimism that this is going to get under control and what does he need or what does he say that he needs going forward.
segments.zh: 你如何评估他对疫情得到控制的乐观程度？他说他需要什么？

segments.en: I think firstly he just wanted protective equipment for the staff secondly he wanted to be able to secure that hospital so that they could work in a safe environment.
segments.zh: 首先，他想要为员工提供防护设备；其次，他希望医院安全，以便在安全的环境中工作。

segments.en: You know when I met that man in the ward the young doctor you know he was just not just exhausted he just come off a night shift where someone had died during the night lady fell into a coma and died.
segments.zh: 我在病房见到那位年轻医生时，他不仅疲惫，刚下夜班，那晚有人去世了——一位女士陷入昏迷后死亡。

segments.en: But you know he really felt like he was at the end of his tether he said we were almost two weeks into this crisis and this is all we have.
segments.zh: 他感到走投无路，他说：疫情已经持续近两周，我们只有这些。

segments.en: How is it possible that both my own government but also this international system that has deployed to so many of these Ebola emergencies.
segments.zh: 怎么可能，我的政府和这个曾应对过多次埃博拉紧急情况的国际体系，都没有行动？

segments.en: He was basically saying why is that not here and that kind of frustration is palpable among many of the health professionals health care professionals you meet in some of these frontline areas.
segments.zh: 他基本上在问：为什么援助没有到位？这种沮丧情绪在前线地区的许多医护人员中显而易见。
